summary:
Items 2, 3, and 4 give ONE decision (D-PRE-11) and four closed things. I wrote drafts only, below /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/round7/decisions/limit-production. The worktree has no change from this lane, and nothing ran against production or with a Cloudflare credential. Loaded skills: ariakit-general-workflow, ariakit-general-markdown.

Item 2 (capture limit): NOT a choice today. Each of the three forms of D54 says "Measure first", so "approve about 20,000 now" is not permitted. The binding ledger line is:

  docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md:462
  "Measure first, then select and document conservative numeric limits under the maintainer's implementation authorization"

The maintainer gave that authorization today. The measurement needs the real code of step 1 of D-DATA-02 (the Node probe builds object shapes only), so it is an implementation task. The number goes to the maintainer one time, in the contract pull request that states it.

Item 3 (reads): ONE decision, with five reads (the four of the record, and one new: the list of the D1 databases). Recommended: the implementation runs 3 wrangler commands of a fixed list, and the two dashboard values are optional looks of the maintainer.

Item 4 (two writes): closed, authorized today. The UPDATE, measured on a local SQLite file with the 33 real migrations (2 rows of 3 accounts changed, second run 0, the 3 sessions stay):

  UPDATE account SET accessToken=NULL,refreshToken=NULL,idToken=NULL,
                     accessTokenExpiresAt=NULL,refreshTokenExpiresAt=NULL
  WHERE providerId='github'
    AND (accessToken IS NOT NULL OR refreshToken IS NOT NULL OR idToken IS NOT NULL
         OR accessTokenExpiresAt IS NOT NULL OR refreshTokenExpiresAt IS NOT NULL);

It runs after the deployment with the token hook, because each sign-in writes the tokens again (packages/security/src/auth.ts:38). A signed-in person notices nothing: the statement does not touch the table session. The measurement of D-SCALE-02 waits with its limit.

Verification: the record build accepts a draft copy of revision r7 with the decision and the 3 fragments ("16 sections, 59 decisions, 568 findings", "0 warning(s). No file was written (--check)"). Each of the 8 evidence ids exists in findings.json. Used id: D-PRE-11. Not used: D-PRE-12 to D-PRE-19.

decisions.question: Who makes the five read-only reads of production that the settled answers need?
decisions.options: (1) no-reads: Nobody reads production. No access, 0 rows written. D-LOAD-02 cannot be built as selected (the hint needs the region), about 900 lines for old data forms stay, the comparison Worker is deleted on code evidence alone. (2) maintainer-reads: You make each read from a list of 3 commands and 2 dashboard pages, about 15 minutes (estimate); the implementation waits for you at two places. (3) commands-by-implementation: the implementation runs 3 wrangler commands of a fixed list (region with `wrangler d1 info visonaut --json`, 5 SELECT count statements in one file, `wrangler d1 list --json`); the two dashboard values (CPU time of one trace, request count of visonaut-compare) are optional looks of the maintainer and the work does not wait for them. (4) all-by-implementation: option 3, and the implementation also opens the two Cloudflare dashboard pages in the Chrome session of the maintainer; risk: that session is the complete Cloudflare account.
decisions.recommended: commands-by-implementation. Evidence: it adds no access, because the authorized UPDATE of D-AUTH-05 uses the same tool and the same login (form of docs/operations/compact-processed-webhooks.md:18-20); 0 rows written, checked through meta.rows_written and meta.changed_db; read 1 (region) is a step of the settled answer D-LOAD-02; the runbook already has read-only SELECT commands for production (docs/baseline-delta-cutover.md:104-110); the two dashboard values decide no settled answer. It is wrong if the maintainer does not want an agent to use his Cloudflare login for more than the two writes, or if this computer has no wrangler login (not checked, because the check uses the login).
decisions.place: Section file apps/lab/audit/content/sections/15-your-answers.html: a new part <h3 id="your-answers-reads"> at the end of the part your-answers-d1, directly before <h3 id="your-answers-compat"> (before line 789 of revision r7). The panel placeholder is the last element of the fragment, after the table of the five reads, the command block, the SQL block, the option table, and the findings. Links to it can come from #dashboard-load-placement, #run-load-inventory, #code-comparison-worker, and #your-answers-compat. Fragment: fragments/D-PRE-11.html.

closed: C1, item 2, the capture limit of one run: not a decision. Closing words: "I authorize the implementation, the GitHub writes, the two writes to production D1, and the package publication and the change in ariakit/ariakit." and "3. Ok". The implementation must: (1) build the service part of step 1 of D-DATA-02 first; (2) measure the real Submit validation and materialization in a Worker runtime (local workerd through miniflare 5.20260921.0-alpha, apps/web/package.json:40) at 3,832, 10,000, 20,000, and 40,000 captures, one Submit and two at the same time, with the heap snapshot method of reports/gap-unexplained-waits/verification.md:252; (3) select a conservative number and state its rule; (4) put it in one setting in place of maximumCaptures: 40_000 (apps/web/src/runtime-defaults.ts:14), with a refusal before the uploads and its own error code (D-OPS-05); (5) state the number, the rule, and the measurement in the contract pull request, which the maintainer reviews and the implementation does not merge alone; (6) state the scope 'local workerd, not hosted'; (7) ask the maintainer first only if the number is below 10,580, the planning number of contract-issue-1.md:340. The record states it in 40-data-storage.html, anchor data-inventory-outside (new words in fragments/closed-C1-data-inventory-outside.html), in one more sentence of the rationale of D-DATA-02, and item 2 leaves the list of section 15.

C2, item 4, the UPDATE of D-AUTH-05: authorized today ("the two writes to production D1"). Table account (apps/web/migrations/0003_auth.sql:6), 5 columns set to NULL, one row for each GitHub account that has a token, which is each person who signed in since the cutover of 2026-10-04 (count not read; assumption: about 10 or fewer). The identity of the row, user, and session stay, so nobody is signed out and a signed-in person notices nothing; no code reads the 5 columns (the only two places set them to NULL: packages/security/src/webhooks.ts:137, apps/web/src/operations/recovery.ts:40). It runs one time, after the deployment with the token hook and the allow-list of D-AUTH-01, with a count before, the UPDATE with one more condition (a second run writes 0), and the same count after with the result 0. The record states it in 30-access-trust.html, anchor access-app (new SQL block and two paragraphs in fragments/closed-C2-access-app.html), and three sentences of section 15 change from 'on your instruction' to 'authorized on 2026-10-07'.

C3, item 4, the measurement for the limit of D-SCALE-02: authorized today, and it waits with its limit, by the note of round 4 "Let's defer this to when this is a problem." Nothing is built now. When the limit is built, the issue of the limit states the exact statements, the row count, the tables, and how the test rows leave the database, and then the measurement runs one time. Estimate from the local D1 formulas: 260,032 rows at 20,000 changes, about 520,000 with the removal, which is 1% of the 50 million rows of one month. The record states it in 40-data-storage.html, anchor data-scale-run (the note before the three panels), in the rationale of D-SCALE-02, and item 4 leaves the list of section 15.

C4, two parts of item 3 that are not in D-PRE-11: the one page load before and after the region hint is a part of the settled answer D-LOAD-02 and a task of that implementation step; the two settings of GitHub App 5028451 (token expiry and device flow) stay a look of the maintainer, as a check box in the implementation issue of D-AUTH-02.
wrongInRecord: D54 is quoted in one of its three forms only. The record says "measure first, then approve numeric limits" (40-data-storage.html:2550-2551 of r7; item 2 of the list). That is the prose of contract-issue-1.md:342. The ledger of the same binding file says "then select and document conservative numeric limits under the maintainer's implementation authorization" (:462). The option that the maintainer selected says "Return with numeric limits" and "remain open until the measured proposal is accepted" (docs/design-r9.json, D54, option measure). D54 is not in docs/current-contract.md (it is binding through line 7), it does not say "in a Worker", and it names no capture count.
D54 sends the record of the limits to issue #61. Read with gh today: issue #61 is closed since 2026-10-01.

D-AUTH-05, the selected option: "After the statement, no route and no database copy can give a GitHub user token." Too strong. D1 Time Travel can restore the rows for 30 days (apps/web/src/operations/README.md:74). The runbook keeps the database from before the cutover for a rollback and the cutover copied no user (docs/baseline-delta-cutover.md:3, :12, :179), so that database, if it still exists, has the stored tokens of the earlier sign-ins and the UPDATE does not reach it. The record names neither copy.

Compatibility table, row "The count of runs with no inventory in production": that count is not a measure of old data. A run of today gets its inventory key in a later statement than the one that creates its row (packages/service/src/run-admission.ts:644). The count needs the condition sealed_at IS NOT NULL.

Compatibility table, row "The count of check rows with the old names in production": D1 stores no check name. The old name shows as an external id that starts with 'ariviso:' (packages/security/src/checks.ts:11, :175). The second old name is the table operations_review_links, and the service still inserts rows there (apps/web/src/operations/review-links.ts:224).

Item 3 and the order of work ("the trace before D-RUN-03") present the trace as a need of D-RUN-03. The trace decides no settled answer today: D-RUN-03 is settled, and the two changes that "wait for the trace" (25-run-load.html:958) are no longer necessary after D-RUN-02 and D-DATA-02. It only divides the server wait into CPU, R2, and GitHub.
Item 3 counts four reads. A fifth is necessary because of the fact about D-AUTH-05: the list of the D1 databases of the account.
doubts: Who accepts the capture limit. I closed item 2 with no panel. The closure depends on one rule that the issues must keep: the implementation does not merge the contract pull request with the number before the maintainer reviewed it. If the coordinator reads the first form of D54 more strictly, the alternative is a decision AFTER the measurement, not today.

The wrangler login. Nobody knows if the wrangler of this computer has a login to the Cloudflare account of Visonaut, or which scopes it has. The recommended option of D-PRE-11 depends on it. I did not check, because the check uses the login.

The API page lists D1 Read as sufficient for the D1 query endpoint. I do not know if a token with D1 Read only can run a statement that writes. If it cannot, such a token is a safer access for the reads than the wrangler login. Not tested.

wrangler d1 info: the API response has running_in_region, but the wrangler page shows no output fields, so I did not confirm that wrangler 4.136.1 prints it. The fallback is meta.served_by_region of one SELECT 1. D1 gives an area such as ENAM, not a cloud region such as aws:us-east-1, so the page load before and after the hint must confirm the value.

The Cloudflare pages were read through a tool that summarizes them, and I did not open the dashboard. The place of the traces and of the metrics in the dashboard is an assumption. So is the inheritance of the top-level observability key by env.production (apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:15-20).

A new cost fact, outside these items: the traces page says that from 2026-12-01 stored traces count in Cloudflare Observability pricing. Production stores a trace for each request (no sampling rate is set). Nobody estimated that cost. It is a candidate for a finding.

The hosted memory of a Worker stays unmeasured. The limit comes from local workerd, and docs/evidence/worker-memory/README.md:3 and :22 say that a local value does not establish a hosted peak. A hosted proof needs a diagnostic Worker with its own D1 and R2, which contract line 188 does not authorize. If the maintainer wants that proof before the limit goes live, it is a new question.

The rule for 'conservative' (two Submits at the same time hold no more than 75% of 128 MB) is my proposal. With the Node values it gives a number below 20,000. Then the texts that say 'about 20,000' (settled answer of D-DATA-02, rationale of D-SCALE-02) follow the measured number.

The authorization of the D-SCALE-02 measurement has no date, and the measurement can run months later with a design that does not exist today. A measurement on a new D1 database would write nothing to production, but a new database is not in the authorization of today.

The database from before the cutover and the preview database (395b539c-c423-4ce4-887c-a5792792a63b) can hold stored tokens. Read 3 of D-PRE-11 shows if they exist, and not if they were cleared. The end of the earlier database is not one of the two authorized writes: if it exists, that is a new question for the maintainer.

The count of accounts that the UPDATE changes is not known ('about 10 or fewer' is an assumption). The 15 minutes for the reads of the maintainer is an estimate with no measurement. The line counts 'about 270' and 'about 150' come from findings PKG-10 and API-14 and were not counted again.

The 5 count statements ran against the 33 migrations in a local SQLite file, not against D1. Two more counts are possible for upload evidence version 2 (storage_version = 2 on ingest_manifests and ingest_run_provenance, 0033_d1_upload_evidence.sql:19-20). I did not add them.

Place of the fragment: section 15 is in work for revision r8, so 'before line 789' is for revision r7 only. I chose section 15 because the five reads belong to four sections. If a topic section is preferred, the nearest one is dashboard-load-placement, because read 1 is the only read that a settled answer cannot do without.
The folder draft/ in my lane folder is a copy of revision r7 with the fragments, made only for the build check. It can be deleted.
